source.title: Rank Measures of Fine-Tuning Updates Need a Noise Baseline

page_placements.theme: Geometry and low-rank proxies do not establish safety-specific mechanisms

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses whether weight-space statistics support claims that post-training is superficial, but it does not measure refusal, harmful compliance, response-token KL, bypasses, or safety behaviour localized to weights.
record.gate_note: The paper reports extensive results on fine-tuning update spectra and model performance after weight edits. Those results concern weight-space rank and general task performance, not the safety behaviours or interventions named by V1–V7. Safety alignment depth is mentioned in related work, including a citation, but is not tested here.
record.test_reason: The study measures rank statistics of weight updates and general task performance (GSM8K, GPQA, perplexity) after edits. It never measures refusal, harmful compliance, per-token KL on harmful prompts, bypasses, or safety behaviour carried by weights. Qi et al. is cited only in related work. Its argument concerns the superficial alignment hypothesis via effective rank of W, which is a different construct from shallow safety alignment.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors add that an edit built on the update's effective rank had no measurable effect on GSM8K or GPQA-Diamond. They also recommend checking bf16 rounding and that checkpoint pairs are really related.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies weight-update spectra and generic task performance, rather than the safety interventions or behavioural measurements in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported degree of concentration depends on the rank measure and, for threshold counts, the chosen singular-value cutoff. Update shape also varies with model and training data.

fits_no_version.finding: Matched SFT, wikitext and code fine-tunes give similar stable ranks of the update (Qwen 0.097/0.093/0.094; SmolLM2 0.025/0.020/0.034), all far below noise (0.436/0.354).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concentration of fine-tuning updates is generic to fine-tuning, not specific to instruction tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: DPO with real labels and the half-swapped control give near-identical stable rank (0.053 vs 0.055) and direction overlap (0.27 vs 0.28 against a second seed).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At modest preference strength, the shape of the DPO update does not depend on learning the preferences.

fits_no_version.finding: Scrambled-word training gives the most concentrated updates (0.042 Qwen, 0.009 SmolLM2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Update concentration depends on the training process and data rather than on alignment content.

fits_no_version.finding: A random update of the same norm leaves eRank(W) nearly unchanged (≤0.5%) but cuts Qwen3-0.6B GSM8K from 59.5% to 4–6%. Timber's eRank-cutoff edit has no measurable effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An unchanged effective rank of weights after post-training cannot show that post-training is superficial.

record.code_released: Code and artifacts are stated to be withheld while the paper is under review; a release is planned.
record.problems: The paper does not measure safety behaviour, refusals, harmful compliance, or token-position KL. Its controlled preference-training experiment uses one model; the authors also note limits on model scale, seeds, and evaluation scope.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported update-rank measurements and general benchmark edit results were not extracted because they do not measure safety behaviour or another named claim version.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning or harmful-request compliance measured.
Benign SFT (Alpaca), wikitext and code fine-tunes are run, but harmful compliance is never measured.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
Update rank and concentration are measured, but no link to safety behaviour is tested.
No test of data or objective as a cause of shallow safety.

record.verdict_notes: All rows are rank measurements, correctly linked to none with state cannot_determine. The study's 'superficial alignment' refers to the Zhou et al./Wu et al. hypothesis, not to safety depth, so no version verdict is given.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning examples and harmful-request compliance.
Whether benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Prefilled openings, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as safety bypasses.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether data or training objectives produce shallow safety behaviour.
Training to deepen safety and its robustness.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The paper discusses shallow alignment and cites early-token safety concentration in related work, without testing safety behaviour.

tranche.reason: Weight-update spectra and general task performance do not measure any V1–V7 safety effect; the paper neither tests nor uses those effects.

source_check.notes: SmolLM2 differences across datasets are real rather than seed noise (§4.3). Matching tokens does not match optimizer steps or loss masking; these rank measurements cannot establish safety localization.
